title: On the Genus Polynomial of Cubic Graphs
summary: The orientable genus polynomial of a graph counts its cellular embeddings by genus. For finite simple $2$-connected cubic graphs it is a cycle-matroid invariant: $M(G)\cong M(H)$ implies $Γ_G=Γ_H$. The adjacency spectrum and the genus polynomial are incomparable: neither determines the other. We exhibit connected cubic graphs on $16$ vertices sharing the adjacency spectrum, spanning-tree count, girth, diameter, vertex and edge connectivity, automorphism-group order, and cycle counts through length $10$, yet with pairwise distinct genus polynomials.
